name: TED Manufacturing Corporation
old_description: Founded in 1956 in Shawnee, Kansas, TED Manufacturing Corporation is a leading designer and manufacturer of RF type coaxial connectors. We specialize in short to medium run custom RF connectors that meet the requirements of our customers. Our connectors in many cases are as or more economically friendly than the off-the-shelf offerings from competitors. Our experienced engineering and production team can assist in developing the connector to fulfill your need.
about:
Founded in 1956 in Shawnee, Kansas, TED Manufacturing Corporation has operated continuously as a designer and manufacturer of RF coaxial connectors. The company is based in Shawnee Mission, Kansas, where it runs an all-inclusive shop that handles machining, plating, heat treating, soft solder, glass seal firing, inspection, assembly, and shipping under one roof.

TED produces custom and standard RF connectors, including BNC, TNC, SMB, and Adapter series, as well as hermetically sealed parts and specialty connectors such as the 104 Series transponder antennas, helical cable removable connectors, fuel-system connectors, and blind self-centering connectors. The company maintains a library of over 11 connector families plus custom designs drawn from 70 years of experience, with roughly half of its shipped volume consisting of custom or modified parts. Engineering support is provided from concept through production.

The company serves aerospace and avionics programs with transponder antennas and hermetic feed-throughs; defense customers with MIL-DTL-38999, BNC, TNC, and N connectors built in ITAR-registered cells; broadcast and telecom operators with tower-rated and weather-sealed cable assemblies, helical assemblies, and 75Ω BNC for SDI video; test and measurement labs with precision connectors through 40 GHz including 3.5 mm, 2.92 mm, and ATE-grade SMA; and industrial and energy sectors with ruggedized connectors for fuel systems.

TED emphasizes that keeping every manufacturing step in-house eliminates lost parts, miscommunication, and overlapping lead times, while using solely USA-sourced materials and components. The company cites restructured pricing and shorter-than-average lead times as key differentiators, and commits to responding to inquiries within one business day.

name: TOA SE, Inc.
old_description: Since 2001, TOA Systems Engineering has provided quality engineering services specializing in control systems, industrial automation, and process optimization. We pride ourselves on delivering innovative solutions that meet the highest standards of quality and safety in the manufacturing industry.
about:
TOA SE, Inc. operates from Nicholasville, Kentucky. The company traces its roots to 1956 when TOA Electronics Company was established in Nagoya, Japan. The U.S. subsidiary, TOA Electric USA, Inc., was founded in Lexington, Kentucky in 2001 to provide factory automation and systems integration for regional manufacturers. In 2007 the business moved to a new facility in Nicholasville and was renamed TOA SE (Systems Engineering); the legal name became TOA SE, Inc. in 2010.

The company designs and builds UL 508A‑certified control panels, provides on‑site programming, modifications and upgrades, and delivers turnkey machine design and build services. Its 27,000‑square‑foot project warehouse supports metal fabrication, post‑machining processing and NC tack‑up work.

TOA SE serves automotive and material‑handling manufacturers. Named customers include Toyota Material Handling, Toyota Motor Manufacturing, General Motors, Honda of America Manufacturing, Michigan Automotive Compressor and Toyotomi America Corporation.

The firm emphasizes a "quick and flexible" approach, with functional‑safety‑certified engineers performing risk assessments and safety upgrades. Its mission is to be the integrator of choice by prioritizing unrivaled quality and safety, meeting deadlines with relentless determination, and operating in an environmentally and financially conscious manner.

name: TOMAR Electronics, Inc.
old_description: TOMAR designs and manufactures signaling, illumination, and control systems trusted by plant managers, first responders, fleet operators, and public safety professionals around the world. Since 1969, we’ve proudly served the emergency, industrial, preemption, off-road, and custom OEM markets with a relentless commitment to quality, innovation, and excellence.
about:
TOMAR Electronics, Inc. was founded in 1969 in Chicago, Illinois, initially producing industrial warning equipment for heavy industry. The company is now headquartered in Gilbert, Arizona, and remains a family-owned and operated private business.

TOMAR designs and manufactures signaling, illumination, and control systems across five divisions: Automotive (visual and audible signaling, illumination, and optical preemption for mobile fleets including fire apparatus, police cruisers, and ambulances), Off-Road (LED light bars, illumination bars, and infrared systems for tactical and military use), Traffic (optical preemption and intersection control solutions for municipalities and traffic engineers), Industrial (strobes, sirens, beacons, and perimeter safety lighting for manufacturing, mining, warehousing, transportation hubs, and energy facilities), and Custom OEM (custom-engineered lighting and control systems, private-labeled devices, and ODM development for robotics, heavy equipment, and defense platforms). All products are engineered and assembled at the company's Gilbert facility, which houses a 100-foot automated photometric light tunnel, goniometer, spectroradiometer, Faraday cage for EMI/EMC testing, environmental chambers, and a full in-house test lab.

The company serves plant managers, first responders, fleet operators, and public safety professionals worldwide. Its customer base spans emergency services, municipal government, traffic engineering, industrial manufacturing, mining, energy, military and defense, off-road vehicle operators, marine, robotics, and heavy equipment OEMs.

TOMAR emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015 certification, 100% burn-in testing, statistical process control, and warranties as quality differentiators. Since 2009 it has operated as an SRP Energy Star-rated manufacturer, powered by a 100 kW rooftop solar array, and pursues climate-conscious operations including energy load shifting and robust recycling.

name: TSMC Washington
old_description: Based in Camas, Washington, USA. TSMC Washington is a wholly-owned subsidiary of TSMC and is one of six TSMC manufacturing sites located around the world. TSMC was founded in 1987 and created the dedicated foundry model. Today, TSMC is the foundry leader in manufacturing capacity, process technology, and customer service.
about:
TSMC Washington, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), operates an 8-inch wafer fabrication facility known as Fab11 in Camas, Washington. TSMC, founded in 1987, pioneered the dedicated foundry model; the Washington site was established as one of six global manufacturing locations to extend that model into the United States.

The facility provides dedicated IC foundry services, including wafer fabrication, test, and analysis capabilities, mirroring the technology and quality standards of TSMC's other 8-inch fabs. With approximately 100 employees, the site supports a broad range of specialty process technologies and has contributed to the production of more than 11,000 distinct products for over 600 customers worldwide.

Customers span the computer, communications, and consumer electronics sectors, relying on TSMC Washington for volume production and quick-turn prototyping. The site serves TSMC's global customer base directly, offering a full array of manufacturing services from design enablement through final test.

The company emphasizes environmental stewardship, having sourced 100 percent renewable energy since 2018 and outfitted its buildings with Energy Star-rated fixtures. Its stated core values—integrity, customer trust, innovation, and commitment—underpin a culture that also prioritizes competitive regional wages and comprehensive health, safety, and supply-chain management programs.

The company produces mission systems, radio frequency (RF) components, RF microwave and microelectronic assemblies, and technologically advanced interconnect products including printed circuit boards (PCBs) and substrates. TTM serves the aerospace and defense sector, including space applications. Its customer base includes organizations requiring mission-critical electronics such as aerospace and defense OEMs, with specific offerings in custom assemblies, microelectronics, and engineered solutions for those markets.

name: Technical Cable Applications, Inc.
old_description: With your specifications, TCA orders any additional parts needed to begin proper cable assembly production. Automation has been developed for aspects of contract cable and harness assembly like automated wire cutting, stripping, crimping, 3D printing, and injection molding. We use automated work instruction systems developed in partnership with Scout Systems, which enable us to not only make our cable manufacturing as efficient as possible, but also improve our processes by letting us identify wasted effort and time more easily. Much of the work is custom and hand made as well, by IPC certified and trained cable technicians when necessary. Our team of technicians are experienced and qualified, and always ensure that every wire and cable they touch is assembled properly and carefully. A tour of our manufacturing facility will show that we are the cable manufacturer to trust as we are extremely rigid about quality control, inventory, and best practices not only to continue meeting our UL certifications which are randomly audited, but also because that's how we've operated our business since being founded in 2002.
about:
Technical Cable Applications, Inc. (TCA) operates from Auburn, Washington, where it was founded in 2002 as a contract cable manufacturer specializing in custom cable assemblies and wire harnesses. The company remains privately held, though ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

TCA produces custom cable assemblies and wire harnesses using a mix of automated and manual processes. Its facility employs robotic despoiling and wire cutting machines, automated stripping and crimping equipment (including a Schleuniger 36SP Crimp Center), 3D printing, injection molding, and MoldMan thermoplastic overmolding machines. The company also runs automated work instruction software developed with Scout Systems. Much of the assembly work is performed by IPC‑certified technicians, and the shop follows IPC/WHMA‑A‑620 Revision E standards. TCA notes it can overmold assemblies “by the thousands,” but does not publish overall headcount or facility square footage.

The company serves medical, aerospace, automotive, electronics, and telecommunications industries. It builds assemblies for applications ranging from medical devices and aircraft wiring to automotive harnesses and industrial Ethernet cables. Customers provide drawings and specifications, and TCA sources connectors from brands such as Molex, TE Connectivity, Hirose, JST, and Mouser.

TCA emphasizes its investment in automation and process control as a differentiator. The Scout Systems work‑instruction platform helps identify wasted effort, while random UL audits and ITAR registration underscore its quality discipline.

name: Techno Metal Post Vermont
old_description: , serving areas across the state, including Burlington, Essex, Shelburne, Charlotte, St. Albans, Newport, White River Junction, and Brattleboro. Since 2016, Zachary has dedicated himself to his career with Techno Metal Post, completing over 1,600 projects ranging from mailboxes and small decks to bike path bridges and residential houses. Although most of his projects are in the residential sector, he has also worked on larger commercial projects. Zachary continues his commitment to making all helical pile projects a reality!
about:
Techno Metal Post Vermont operates from Montpelier, Vermont, where Zachary LaPorte established the dealership in 2016. As a certified installer in the Techno Metal Post network, LaPorte brought the Canadian helical-pile system to Vermont builders and property owners, starting with smaller residential jobs and expanding to larger structural foundations.

The company installs steel helical piles for permanent and temporary foundations, using specialized hydraulic equipment designed and manufactured by the parent company in Quebec. Services include site evaluation, engineering support, and pile installation for decks, porches, additions, homes, garages, and commercial structures. Since 2016 the Vermont dealership has completed more than 1,600 projects across the state, from mailbox footings to bike-path bridges and full residential houses.

Customers span residential, commercial, and industrial sectors throughout Vermont, including the Burlington, Essex, Shelburne, Charlotte, St. Albans, Newport, White River Junction, and Brattleboro areas. The dealership works directly with homeowners, contractors, engineers, and municipalities, providing engineered foundation solutions for difficult soil conditions and limited-access sites.

LaPorte cites the backing of Techno Metal Post's 30-year history, ISO 9001-certified manufacturing, and an in-house engineering department launched in 1998 as key differentiators. Every installer in the network completes intensive theoretical and hands-on certification, and the Vermont operation draws on that support for design review and load calculations on each project.

name: Thermoplastic Processes
old_description: With over 75 years of experience, Thermoplastic Processes stands as a premier manufacturer of fabricated and extruded plastics, offering a diverse range including thermoplastic tubing, PVC pipe, and more.
about:
Thermoplastic Processes was founded in 1951 in Georgetown, Delaware. The company operates as a subsidiary of TPI Partners Corporation and has spent over seven decades developing extruded and fabricated plastic products.

The company manufactures a broad line of plastic tubing, rods, pipe, and profiles through extrusion and fabrication processes. Its catalog includes more than 5,000 stock-keeping units across over a dozen material families, such as PVC, polyethylene, polyurethane, nylon, acrylic, polycarbonate, and platinum-cured silicone. Standard items are kept in inventory for immediate shipment, and custom sizes, lengths, and colors are produced to order.

Thermoplastic Processes serves the food and beverage, industrial and chemical, laboratory, and medical sectors, including medical disposables. Its products are used in beverage dispensing, pharmaceutical production, chemical handling, and laboratory fluid transfer, among other applications.

The company positions itself as a cost-effective alternative to branded tubing such as Tygon®, Klearon™, and ClearFLEX™, offering equivalent replacements at lower cost. Its stated mission emphasizes superior service through a dedicated team and a commitment to quality.

name: Trayer Engineering Corporation
old_description: Trayer Engineering (a Siemens company) manufactures high-reliability medium-voltage electrical switchgear (padmount, submersible, vaultmount) and related control equipment. Products are custom-built for utility, industrial and communications power applications. ISO 9001:2015 certified; switchgear is UL-listed (UL 891).
about:
Trayer Engineering Corporation operates from San Leandro, California, where it was founded in 1962 as a pioneer in low-maintenance vacuum switchgear for electrical distribution systems. Now a Siemens company, the business is led by CEO Kevin Calister and continues to design and manufacture its products at its California headquarters.

The company produces medium-voltage switchgear in padmount, submersible, and vaultmount configurations, along with solid-dielectric models, automatic transfer switches, and automation controls for SCADA, microgrid, and smart-grid applications. Its designs feature fully sealed, welded-seam construction in corrosion-resistant 304 stainless steel, patented Tri-Phase visible disconnects, and a 20 kA symmetrical fault-current rating. and 25 international representatives.

Primary customers include electric utilities, telecommunications providers, oil and gas operators, and industrial power-distribution firms. Products are custom-built for each application, ranging from utility distribution automation to hardened infrastructure for storm-prone regions.

The company cites its patented Tri-Phase two-position visible disconnect, internal ground position, and mechanical VFI trip indicators as features that simplify operation and increase reliability in harsh environments.

name: Tri-Mack Plastics Manufacturing Corporation
old_description: Since it was founded in 1974, Tri-Mack has supplied the aerospace industry with precision thermoplastic components. Our quality system has been built to support the needs of aerospace OEMs as reflected by our AS9100 certification. We are proud to be recognized by customers such as GE Aerospace, who presented us with Best in Class and Supplier Quality Awareness awards.
about:
Tri-Mack Plastics Manufacturing Corporation was founded in 1974 in Bristol, Rhode Island. The company began as a supplier of precision thermoplastic components to the aerospace industry.

The company provides vertically integrated manufacturing services including thermoplastic composites processing, injection molding, CNC machining, engineering support, and material selection. Its capabilities span from concept through production, with in-house quality inspection using CMMs, ultrasonic NDT, and in-machine probing on CNC milling centers.

Tri-Mack serves aerospace, defense, industrial, and medical markets. Aerospace OEMs such as GE Aerospace have recognized the company with Best in Class and Supplier Quality Awareness awards. Defense customers rely on the firm for precision components meeting complex regulatory standards. Industrial clients use materials like Victrex PEEK, Torlon PAI, Ultem PEI, and Ryton PPS for equipment assemblies. Medical equipment manufacturers depend on Tri-Mack for components that ensure accuracy and meet rigorous regulatory requirements.

The company differentiates itself through a quality management system certified to AS9100, ISO 9001, and NADCAP, which governs lot traceability, material certifications, and approved vendor requirements. On-staff designated supplier quality representatives (DSQRs) enable direct ship-to-stock for many customers. Vertically integrated capabilities and engineering collaboration aim to optimize parts for manufacturability from concept through delivery.
